heap-build.title: Bottom-up min/max heap construction
preconditions: Values are integers; logical length is in 0..32. maximum=false selects a min-heap; true selects a max-heap.
Mutation operations assume an existing heap; heap_build/heapBuild is included for explicit setup. C and Java use a capacity buffer plus logical length; vector/list/Array use their current length.
notes: Example implementation; choosing a language does not change visualization execution.

heap-insert.title: Append and sift upward
preconditions: Values are integers; logical length is in 0..32. maximum=false selects a min-heap; true selects a max-heap.
Mutation operations assume an existing heap; heap_build/heapBuild is included for explicit setup. C and Java use a capacity buffer plus logical length; vector/list/Array use their current length.
notes: Example implementation; choosing a language does not change visualization execution.
Equal priorities do not promise stable ordering. Strict comparisons choose the left child on ties.
Preparation is O(n) and is separate from the per-operation bound.
heap-insert.time: O(log n) sift with reserved capacity; a dynamic collection can take O(n) when reallocating
heap-insert.space: O(1) sifting state; growable collection reallocation may use O(n) storage

rec-factorial.title: Factorial with a safe finite contract
preconditions: Integer n in 0..12; 12! fits signed 32-bit range. Invalid n is rejected.
notes: Example implementation; choosing a language does not change visualization execution.

rec-sum.title: Recursive sum of a prefix
preconditions: 0≤n≤32 and n≤array length; |value|≤100000. The input is not modified.
notes: Example implementation; choosing a language does not change visualization execution.

rec-binary.title: Recursive inclusive binary search
preconditions: Input is sorted ascending and length≤32. Call with lo=0, hi=length-1. Bounds describe a valid subrange, including an empty crossed interval.
Returns any matching index or -1. The visualization checks sortedness; these functions assume it rather than adding a linear scan to each recursive call.
notes: Example implementation; choosing a language does not change visualization execution.

rec-fibonacci.title: Branching Fibonacci without memoization
preconditions: Integer n in 0..10. Repeated subproblems are intentionally recomputed to illustrate total calls versus active depth.
notes: Example implementation; choosing a language does not change visualization execution.

two-pair.title: Opposite pointers for sorted pair sum
preconditions: Input is sorted ascending, length≤32 and |value|,|target|≤100000. Sortedness is a prerequisite, not silently repaired.
Two distinct indices are returned; no solution uses (-1,-1) or null/None. Cast before addition in fixed-width examples.
notes: Example implementation; choosing a language does not change visualization execution.

two-reverse.title: Reverse by swapping endpoints
preconditions: Array length≤32; no sorting precondition. Mutates the original array.
notes: Example implementation; choosing a language does not change visualization execution.

two-unique.title: Compact a sorted distinct prefix
preconditions: Input is sorted ascending, length≤32. Returns logical output length; physical capacity and suffix contents remain unchanged.
notes: Example implementation; choosing a language does not change visualization execution.

window-fixed.title: Maximum sum of exactly k values
preconditions: 1≤k≤n≤32; |value|≤100000, including negative values. Strict improvement retains the first best window.
C invalid input returns start=-1; other languages raise an argument/range error.
notes: Example implementation; choosing a language does not change visualization execution.

window-variable.title: Shortest nonnegative window reaching a target
preconditions: n≤32, 0≤value≤100000 and positive target≤100000. No solution is (length=0,start=-1).
Invalid negative inputs/targets are rejected. A 64-bit sum is used in fixed-width examples; lab bounds keep JavaScript Number additions exact.
notes: Example implementation; choosing a language does not change visualization execution.

hash-chain.title: Complete integer map: separate chaining
preconditions: Integer keys and values in ±100000. Initialize an empty map first; these example maps hold up to 32 distinct keys, with capacity 8..64. The interactive input has at most 16 initial pairs plus one operation.
Duplicate insertion updates; missing lookup is distinct from a stored zero. Probing stops after at most capacity inspections.
notes: Chaining C allocates nodes and requires map_free after successful map_init. C++ vectors own their entries; Java/Python/JavaScript use managed storage.
The C lookup returns a success boolean and writes an output parameter. Other examples use optional/null/None for missing integer values.
Rehashing recomputes buckets and removes tombstones. The live-load threshold is 0.75.
Chaining examples with collection buckets may shift a bucket list on deletion; the C linked representation unlinks nodes. Both traverse colliding keys, with linear worst-case bucket work.
hash-chain.time: Expected O(1) under distribution/load assumptions; O(n) worst-case operation; rehash O(n+capacity)
hash-chain.space: O(n+capacity) map storage; rehash temporarily holds old and new storage
